In the following appendix , we derive the entropy of adsorption in the case of infinite dilution and show how it may be related to familiar thermodynamic quantities ( cf . eq 5 ) . To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via $$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$ $$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$ where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. descriptor_candidate.name: molecule_to_path_included_sphere_ratio
descriptor_candidate.hypothesis: If rotational confinement drives part of the adsorption entropy loss, then for frameworks and adsorbates otherwise held fixed, the entropy loss (Sgas-Sads)/R increases when the adsorbate's largest heavy-atom pair distance GeDi grows relative to the framework's largest included sphere along the free-sphere path lsd_p, because a longer molecule has less rotational freedom inside a pore whose included free-path sphere it nearly fills.
descriptor_candidate.rationale: The reported FER/FAU comparison (E02) links smaller cavity diameter to larger rotational entropy loss, and the MFI/FAU comparison (E01, E04) reports larger rotational degrees-of-freedom loss in the tighter framework. Here lsd_p (Zeo++ Dif, the largest included sphere along the free-sphere path) is used as a one-sided geometric proxy for the local confinement scale along the diffusion path; GeDi proxies the adsorbate's maximum rotational span. Their dimensionless ratio encodes a size-mismatch mechanism: near-unity (or larger) ratios indicate the molecule's heavy-atom span approaches the included free-path sphere, plausibly suppressing rotational motion. This is a new combination of an adsorbate geometry proxy with a framework free-path descriptor; neither source supplies fitted coefficients, so no universal constant is assumed. Known limitation: Dif is neither the bottleneck Df nor the global cavity diameter Di used in the source discussion, and GeDi is a heavy-atom (implicit-H) pair distance that ignores hydrogen extent; the mapping to rotational entropy loss is therefore an empirical proxy hypothesis, not an established relation.
descriptor_candidate.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if, holding lsd_p and the fixed references constant, residual entropy loss does not increase with GeDi in the training support, or if the descriptor's association disappears when the competing explanation of translational/vibrational confinement (pore accessibility AV, bottleneck lsd_f) is accounted for; additionally, if the descriptor correlates with loss only through lsd_f-driven diffusion constraints rather than the included-sphere confinement, the rotational confinement interpretation is rejected.

Nevertheless, there remain caveats. review_issues.explanation: E02 attributes the reported confinement effect to the 'average cavity diameter' (FER ~4.3 A vs FAU ~13 A). The draft substitutes lsd_f, the Zeo++ Df largest passing free sphere, which is a window/bottleneck quantity, not the cavity diameter Di referenced by the source. No evidence item reports Df for MFI/FAU or FER/FAU, so mapping the cavity-diameter mechanism onto the Df bottleneck proxy is an unverified transfer under C1/C2, not demonstrated source support.

GeDi is the largest heavy-atom pair distance (an end-to-end span) in an implicit-H, heavy-atom representation; it is not the molecular cross-section that must physically pass through a pore window. Consequently GeDi/lsd_f = 1 is not a physical passage or confinement threshold, ratio values greater than 1 do not imply the molecule cannot pass, and the numerical magnitude of the ratio has no calibrated physical meaning.

Fifty-four training adsorbates are single-site cases with legitimate GeDi = 0, giving descriptor value exactly 0. The conditional prediction (larger GeDi at fixed lsd_f implies larger entropy loss over R) assigns these rows zero confinement signal, yet per E02 confinement-dependent rotational entropy loss exists even for the smallest guests in small-pore frameworks; for these rows the heavy-atom span proxy carries no confinement information by construction.

The held-fixed prediction varies only lsd_f with GeDi fixed, but Df (window bottleneck) does not separate window size from cavity size: a small-window/large-cage framework would produce a large GeDi/lsd_f while exhibiting weak rotational confinement under the cavity-diameter mechanism of E02. E01/E04 mix rotational-DOF loss and total gas-phase entropy loss (38% vs 20% in MFI vs FAU), and E03 adds translational contributions the ratio does not represent. The monotone prediction is therefore mechanism-ambiguous; the derivative check (nonzero fraction 0.977, opposite_n = 0) reflects smooth ratio behavior, not validated mechanism.

E01-E04 do not resolve temperature, loading, or framework chemistry, and the reported factors (3-fold rotational loss; 38%/20% entropy loss fractions) are source-specific and correctly excluded from the formula. Directional transfer to this benchmark's frameworks is conditional only (C1-C4). E06 shows rotational-freedom effects were only 'qualitatively analyzed' for MCM-22 supercages, indicating no source provides quantitative support for a span/bottleneck ratio descriptor.

The only structured limit test covers lsd_f -> positive infinity (ratio -> 0). The opposite limit, lsd_f -> 0+, drives the ratio to unbounded values while GeDi remains bounded (max 10.97 A on training support). Whether the descriptor should saturate and how unbounded values should be interpreted is unspecified; training support (lsd_f >= 0.85684 A) does not cover this regime, so the limit is formally defined but physically uncalibrated.

The knowledge graph contains no edge asserting a measured or validated correlation between GeDi, lsd_f, or their ratio and the entropy loss target in this dataset; all mechanism-to-proxy links are MAY_USE_PROXY_UNDER_ASSUMPTIONS, and no target values are provided. This absent support is unknown, not disproof, but it means the descriptor's empirical validity is entirely untested here.

final_candidate.name: span_over_included_path_sphere
final_candidate.hypothesis: Conditional physical hypothesis: holding the adsorbate heavy-atom enclosing radius SPAN fixed, frameworks with a larger largest included sphere along the free-sphere path (lsd_p, Dif) offer more local space along the adsorption pathway, so adsorbates retain more rotational freedom and the entropy loss over R decreases; equivalently, smaller included-along-path spheres relative to the molecular span increase the rotational entropy loss over R. Conversely, at fixed framework lsd_p, a larger adsorbate enclosing radius SPAN increases the entropy loss over R. This extends the reported cavity-size/rotational-entropy relation (E01, E02, E04) and the MCM-22 supercage radius-of-gyration-versus-available-space argument (E06) to the Dif proxy; it is a proxy-level rotational confinement hypothesis, not an exact free-volume or cavity law.
final_candidate.rationale: SPAN is the heavy-atom enclosing radius about the center of mass in the implicit-H/heavy-atom representation, so it is an upper-bound proxy for the rotor's spatial extent, not an all-atom radius of gyration; legitimate zeros exist for the 54 single-site adsorbates. lsd_p (Zeo++ Dif) is the largest included sphere ALONG the free-sphere path; it is neither the global cavity diameter Di invoked in E02 nor the passing bottleneck Df, so the mapping 'Dif ~ local rotational space along the adsorption pathway' is an empirical proxy choice, not an established equivalence. The ratio is dimensionless and finite on the training support, but no value of 1 has a physical equality meaning under this normalization-free construction. Mechanism: rotational degrees of freedom of a confined molecule are restricted when available space along the pathway approaches the molecular span (E06); the descriptor increases as this available space shrinks or as the molecular span grows.
final_candidate.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if, holding all other actually used native inputs (SPAN, lsd_p) fixed, the entropy loss over R does not increase with SPAN/lsd_p within the training quantile range of lsd_p (3.3452-15.5604 angstrom) and SPAN (0-6.241 angstrom). For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. Although these simulations are numerically cleaner compared to experiment because they involve analyzing efficiently a greater number of molecule–zeolite combinations, it remains overwhelming to apply them to the millions of hypothetical frameworks. Novel topology-based, data-driven approaches have been shown to be adequate in predicting specific features such as adsorption capacity $ ^{6} $ and selectivity. $ ^{26} $ However, there are currently no similar models for entropy.

draft.hypothesis: Conditional physical hypothesis: holding the adsorbate heavy-atom enclosing radius SPAN fixed, frameworks with a larger largest included sphere along the free-sphere path (lsd_p, Dif) offer more local space along the adsorption pathway, so adsorbates retain more rotational freedom and the entropy loss over R decreases; equivalently, smaller included-along-path spheres relative to the molecular span increase the rotational entropy loss over R. Conversely, at fixed framework lsd_p, a larger adsorbate enclosing radius SPAN increases the entropy loss over R. This extends the reported cavity-size/rotational-entropy relation (E01, E02, E04) and the MCM-22 supercage radius-of-gyration-versus-available-space argument (E06) to the Dif proxy; it is a proxy-level rotational confinement hypothesis, not an exact free-volume or cavity law.
draft.rationale: SPAN is the heavy-atom enclosing radius about the center of mass in the implicit-H/heavy-atom representation, so it is an upper-bound proxy for the rotor's spatial extent, not an all-atom radius of gyration; legitimate zeros exist for the 54 single-site adsorbates. lsd_p (Zeo++ Dif) is the largest included sphere ALONG the free-sphere path; it is neither the global cavity diameter Di invoked in E02 nor the passing bottleneck Df, so the mapping 'Dif ~ local rotational space along the adsorption pathway' is an empirical proxy choice, not an established equivalence. The ratio is dimensionless and finite on the training support, but no value of 1 has a physical equality meaning under this normalization-free construction. Mechanism: rotational degrees of freedom of a confined molecule are restricted when available space along the pathway approaches the molecular span (E06); the descriptor increases as this available space shrinks or as the molecular span grows.
draft.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if, holding all other actually used native inputs (SPAN, lsd_p) fixed, the entropy loss over R does not increase with SPAN/lsd_p within the training quantile range of lsd_p (3.3452-15.5604 angstrom) and SPAN (0-6.241 angstrom). review_issues.explanation: The draft maps E02's 'average cavity diameter' onto lsd_p (Zeo++ Dif), but per the input definition Dif is the largest included sphere ALONG the free-sphere path and is explicitly NOT the global cavity diameter Di and NOT the passing bottleneck Df. The hypothesis itself acknowledges this ('not an established equivalence'), but the transfer remains an unjustified proxy substitution: Dif characterizes the diffusion pathway, not necessarily the local space at the adsorption site where rotational restriction occurs. A molecule adsorbing in a large cage connected through a narrow window would have a small Dif without small local rotational space at the site.

E06's argument compares the radius of gyration of each molecule to the available space in the MCM-22 supercage. SPAN is the heavy-atom enclosing radius about the center of mass in an implicit-H/heavy-atom representation, not a radius of gyration (which is mass-weighted and rms-based) and not an all-atom size. SPAN is a monotone-related but distinct quantity; the draft correctly labels it an 'upper-bound proxy' but the mapping radius-of-gyration -> enclosing radius is a second unverified proxy layered on top of the Dif mapping.

E07 derives adsorption entropy at infinite dilution for rigid molecules as Q = Q_trans * Q_rot * Z, with Q_trans and Q_rot described as 'unaffected by confinement' and confinement effects entering through the configurational partition function Z. This formalism is in tension with the draft's mechanism that rotational degrees of freedom are directly restricted by a size ratio. The draft's rotational-confinement hypothesis is a proxy-level extension of E01/E02/E04/E06, not something E07's derivation supports; E07 neither confirms nor refutes it, and the draft should not be read as mechanistically validated by it.

E06 is specific to MCM-22 supercages (closed cages; adsorption predominantly inside supercages) and is embedded in a discussion involving diffusion at 450-850 K. Transfer of the 'radius of gyration vs available space' argument to channel-like frameworks and to the benchmark regime is conditional, as stated in source_conditions C6; the draft cites E06 as motivation but the closed-cage geometry differs from bottleneck/pathway-controlled frameworks where Dif is most informative.

Redundancy risk with the round-2 appended descriptor GeDi/lsd_f: SPAN and GeDi are correlated heavy-atom size proxies (both have zero_n = 54 on identical rows and similar quantile structure), and lsd_p vs lsd_f are related Zeo++ sphere diameters of the same pore system. SPAN/lsd_p is a new combination, but no evidence in the provided inputs establishes that it carries information independent of GeDi/lsd_f; the falsification criteria flag this competing explanation but the review records it as an unresolved scientific issue, not a disproof.

The stated prediction (loss over R decreases as lsd_p increases at fixed SPAN) is consistent with the descriptor direction (SPAN/lsd_p decreases in lsd_p), but the underlying direction claim rests on the Dif-as-local-rotational-space proxy discussed above, which the mechanism cards treat as conditional. The physical prediction is therefore proxy-consistent but unvalidated; 'unverified' scientific consistency in the execution check is appropriate and no causal claim should be recorded.

SPAN = 0 for the 54 single-site training rows is a legitimate representation zero and yields descriptor value 0, correctly not imputed. However, under the hypothesis descriptor 0 would correspond to 'no rotational confinement', which is a semantic edge case for point-like rotor proxies rather than a physical statement; the monotonic confinement claim is only interpretable on SPAN > 0. No division-by-zero risk exists since lsd_p has no zeros in training (min 3.3452 angstrom).

The ratio SPAN/lsd_p can exceed 1 on the training support (SPAN max 6.2408 vs lsd_p min 3.3452). Under the stated rules no value of 1 carries a physical equality threshold meaning here, since SPAN is a heavy-atom upper-bound proxy and Dif is a probe-based pathway quantity; any interpretation of ratio 1 as 'molecule exactly fits' would be an error, and the draft correctly avoids it.

The knowledge graph contains no MAY_USE_PROXY_UNDER_ASSUMPTIONS edge from any mechanism node to SPAN (edges to size proxies go to GeDi, PMI1-3, Vol, AV). Graph support for SPAN as a rotational-extent proxy is therefore unknown; per the task, this absent edge is unknown support, not disproof of the proxy or mechanism, and is recorded as an open item.

No target values for entropy_loss_over_R are provided, and source percentages in E01/E02/E04 (e.g., 38% vs 20% loss; 3-fold rotational loss) are report-specific and must not be imported as constants or used to calibrate the descriptor's scale. Whether the reported MFI/FAU and FER/FAU comparisons transfer to this benchmark's frameworks and regime remains unresolved.

draft.name: span_over_included_path_sphere
draft.hypothesis: Conditional physical hypothesis: holding the adsorbate heavy-atom enclosing radius SPAN fixed, frameworks with a larger largest included sphere along the free-sphere path (lsd_p, Dif) offer more local space along the adsorption pathway, so adsorbates retain more rotational freedom and the entropy loss over R decreases; equivalently, smaller included-along-path spheres relative to the molecular span increase the rotational entropy loss over R. Conversely, at fixed framework lsd_p, a larger adsorbate enclosing radius SPAN increases the entropy loss over R. This extends the reported cavity-size/rotational-entropy relation (E01, E02, E04) and the MCM-22 supercage radius-of-gyration-versus-available-space argument (E06) to the Dif proxy; it is a proxy-level rotational confinement hypothesis, not an exact free-volume or cavity law.
draft.rationale: SPAN is the heavy-atom enclosing radius about the center of mass in the implicit-H/heavy-atom representation, so it is an upper-bound proxy for the rotor's spatial extent, not an all-atom radius of gyration; legitimate zeros exist for the 54 single-site adsorbates. lsd_p (Zeo++ Dif) is the largest included sphere ALONG the free-sphere path; it is neither the global cavity diameter Di invoked in E02 nor the passing bottleneck Df, so the mapping 'Dif ~ local rotational space along the adsorption pathway' is an empirical proxy choice, not an established equivalence. The ratio is dimensionless and finite on the training support, but no value of 1 has a physical equality meaning under this normalization-free construction. Mechanism: rotational degrees of freedom of a confined molecule are restricted when available space along the pathway approaches the molecular span (E06); the descriptor increases as this available space shrinks or as the molecular span grows.
draft.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if, holding all other actually used native inputs (SPAN, lsd_p) fixed, the entropy loss over R does not increase with SPAN/lsd_p within the training quantile range of lsd_p (3.3452-15.5604 angstrom) and SPAN (0-6.241 angstrom). A competing explanation that must be tested: the loss may instead track the global cavity diameter Di or the passing bottleneck Df (as in the prior GeDi/lsd_f descriptor), in which case Dif carries no independent rotational-confinement information and the descriptor would be redundant with GeDi/lsd_f rather than falsified on sign alone.

draft_check.reason: Wrong physical variable mapping: lsd_p requires included_along_free_path_Dif

review_issues.explanation: The draft maps E02's 'average cavity diameter' onto lsd_p (Zeo++ Dif), but per the input definition Dif is the largest included sphere ALONG the free-sphere path and is explicitly NOT the global cavity diameter Di and NOT the passing bottleneck Df. The hypothesis itself acknowledges this ('not an established equivalence'), but the transfer remains an unjustified proxy substitution: Dif characterizes the diffusion pathway, not necessarily the local space at the adsorption site where rotational restriction occurs. A molecule adsorbing in a large cage connected through a narrow window would have a small Dif without small local rotational space at the site.

E06's argument compares the radius of gyration of each molecule to the available space in the MCM-22 supercage. SPAN is the heavy-atom enclosing radius about the center of mass in an implicit-H/heavy-atom representation, not a radius of gyration (which is mass-weighted and rms-based) and not an all-atom size. SPAN is a monotone-related but distinct quantity; the draft correctly labels it an 'upper-bound proxy' but the mapping radius-of-gyration -> enclosing radius is a second unverified proxy layered on top of the Dif mapping.

E07 derives adsorption entropy at infinite dilution for rigid molecules as Q = Q_trans * Q_rot * Z, with Q_trans and Q_rot described as 'unaffected by confinement' and confinement effects entering through the configurational partition function Z. This formalism is in tension with the draft's mechanism that rotational degrees of freedom are directly restricted by a size ratio. The draft's rotational-confinement hypothesis is a proxy-level extension of E01/E02/E04/E06, not something E07's derivation supports; E07 neither confirms nor refutes it, and the draft should not be read as mechanistically validated by it.

E06 is specific to MCM-22 supercages (closed cages; adsorption predominantly inside supercages) and is embedded in a discussion involving diffusion at 450-850 K. Transfer of the 'radius of gyration vs available space' argument to channel-like frameworks and to the benchmark regime is conditional, as stated in source_conditions C6; the draft cites E06 as motivation but the closed-cage geometry differs from bottleneck/pathway-controlled frameworks where Dif is most informative.

Redundancy risk with the round-2 appended descriptor GeDi/lsd_f: SPAN and GeDi are correlated heavy-atom size proxies (both have zero_n = 54 on identical rows and similar quantile structure), and lsd_p vs lsd_f are related Zeo++ sphere diameters of the same pore system. SPAN/lsd_p is a new combination, but no evidence in the provided inputs establishes that it carries information independent of GeDi/lsd_f; the falsification criteria flag this competing explanation but the review records it as an unresolved scientific issue, not a disproof.

The stated prediction (loss over R decreases as lsd_p increases at fixed SPAN) is consistent with the descriptor direction (SPAN/lsd_p decreases in lsd_p), but the underlying direction claim rests on the Dif-as-local-rotational-space proxy discussed above, which the mechanism cards treat as conditional. The physical prediction is therefore proxy-consistent but unvalidated; 'unverified' scientific consistency in the execution check is appropriate and no causal claim should be recorded.

SPAN = 0 for the 54 single-site training rows is a legitimate representation zero and yields descriptor value 0, correctly not imputed. However, under the hypothesis descriptor 0 would correspond to 'no rotational confinement', which is a semantic edge case for point-like rotor proxies rather than a physical statement; the monotonic confinement claim is only interpretable on SPAN > 0. No division-by-zero risk exists since lsd_p has no zeros in training (min 3.3452 angstrom).

The ratio SPAN/lsd_p can exceed 1 on the training support (SPAN max 6.2408 vs lsd_p min 3.3452). Under the stated rules no value of 1 carries a physical equality threshold meaning here, since SPAN is a heavy-atom upper-bound proxy and Dif is a probe-based pathway quantity; any interpretation of ratio 1 as 'molecule exactly fits' would be an error, and the draft correctly avoids it.

The knowledge graph contains no MAY_USE_PROXY_UNDER_ASSUMPTIONS edge from any mechanism node to SPAN (edges to size proxies go to GeDi, PMI1-3, Vol, AV). Graph support for SPAN as a rotational-extent proxy is therefore unknown; per the task, this absent edge is unknown support, not disproof of the proxy or mechanism, and is recorded as an open item.

No target values for entropy_loss_over_R are provided, and source percentages in E01/E02/E04 (e.g., 38% vs 20% loss; 3-fold rotational loss) are report-specific and must not be imported as constants or used to calibrate the descriptor's scale. Whether the reported MFI/FAU and FER/FAU comparisons transfer to this benchmark's frameworks and regime remains unresolved.

appended.name: confinement_ratio_GeDi_over_Df
appended.hypothesis: Conditional physical hypothesis: holding the adsorbate heavy-atom span GeDi fixed, frameworks with a smaller largest passing free sphere Df (hence a larger GeDi/lsd_f ratio) confine the adsorbate more tightly, and per the reported MFI-vs-FAU and FER-vs-FAU comparisons (E01, E02, E04) the entropy loss over R increases. Conversely, at fixed framework Df, a larger adsorbate span GeDi increases the entropy loss over R. This is a proxy-level size-versus-bottleneck confinement hypothesis for translational and rotational degrees of freedom (E03); it is not claimed to be an exact free-volume law.
appended.rationale: The mechanism family is confinement-driven rotational/translational entropy loss reported for zeolites (E01-E04), conditioned on C1/C2/C3/C4 transfer assumptions. GeDi is the largest heavy-atom pair distance in an implicit-H representation, so it underestimates the full all-atom cross-section relevant to squeezing through a pore window; it is a geometric proxy, not a measured free-energy barrier. lsd_f is the Zeo++ Df bottleneck (largest passing sphere along a periodic free path), NOT the global cavity diameter Di and NOT the included-along-path Dif; using it as the confinement length is an empirical mapping justified only under the C1/C2 assumptions. The ratio is dimensionless and well-defined on training support (lsd_f min 0.857 A > 0), and legitimate GeDi zeros (54 single-site cases) yield descriptor value 0, preserving physical zeros without imputation. No fitted constants, source percentages, or target statistics enter the formula.
appended.falsification_criteria: The descriptor is falsified for this dataset if: (1) the conditional prediction shows entropy loss over R DECREASING as GeDi/lsd_f increases (e.g., because Df conflates window bottleneck with cage size, so small-window/large-cage frameworks reverse the trend expected from the cavity-diameter mechanism of E02); (2) single-atom or near-zero-GeDi adsorbates show entropy loss comparable to extended adsorbates, indicating the heavy-atom span proxy carries no confinement signal; or (3) a competing explanation such as probe-accessible volume AV or specific area ASA dominates the held-fixed prediction, showing the bottleneck ratio adds no independent information.
appended.proxy_assumptions: Assumes: (a) GeDi (implicit-H heavy-atom representation) is a usable proxy for the molecular dimension governing confinement at pore windows; (b) lsd_f (Df) proxies the confinement length scale, which differs from cavity diameter Di and included-along-path Dif; (c) the reported MFI/FAU and FER/FAU entropy-loss patterns transfer conditionally to this benchmark's frameworks at unspecified temperature and loading; (d) the ratio is an empirical geometric proxy, not a physical equality threshold and not a fitted free-volume quantity. No causal or quantitative universality is established.
appended.boundary_behavior: Finite training support: GeDi in [0, 10.97181443] A (54 legitimate zeros for single-site cases yield descriptor 0), lsd_f in [0.85684, 7.68726] A (strictly positive, so the ratio is defined everywhere on training support). No division by zero occurs; native zeros are preserved rather than imputed.
